summary: Latency regression: p95/p99 spikes for continuous batching causing request timeouts
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-01 09:15 UTC NimbusAI has reported elevated p95/p99 inference latency and intermittent request timeouts for production traffic on dedicated capacity in us-east. Impact: customer reports user-facing timeouts (504) and increased tail latency for real-time features. Environment: Dedicated pool nimbus-prod-us-east, hosts on g4dn-like fleet, models redwood-7b-v1 and redwood-14b-quantized. Observed: p50 stable, p95 and p99 show large spikes correlating with batch wait time increases.
impact: Customer-facing timeouts for live product features (search summarization), increased error budget consumption for dedicated contract, reported by customer as ongoing between 09:15-11:30 UTC. Estimated affected requests: ~8-12% of traffic experienced >2s latency, ~1% timed out.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of short prompt requests (~25-50 tokens) at 80rps to redwood-7b-v1 on the customer's dedicated route
2) Observe latency distribution in traces/metrics over 30m window
3) Look for batch_wait_time_ms and batch_size distributions at the serving runtime
5) Reproduce in staging by replaying production traffic (see runbook)
observed_behavior: p95/p99 latency increased from ~220ms/480ms to spikes up to 1.8s and 3.2s respectively. Intermittent 504s when request TTL exceeded after streaming disconnects.
expected_behavior: Tail latency should remain within SLO (<600ms p99) and no customer request timeouts under normal load.
logs: 2026-03-01T09:27:54Z - request_id=rdw-9f4c - route=nimbus-prod-us-east - error=504 - stream_disconnect=true - batch_wait_time=2500ms - batch_size=1
investigation_notes: 09:25 UTC - Support triaged: correlated spikes with increased batch_wait_time_ms in serving-runtime metrics; batch_size concurrently decreased at tail
09:40 UTC - SRE alerted: sudden rise in scheduler queue length; host CPU and network utilization within normal bounds; no GPU OOMs observed

10:05 UTC - Hypothesis A: recent scheduler tuning (PR #2894) modified the continuous batching timer/threshold causing batches to wait longer before executing in low-concurrency tails, increasing tail latency.

10:20 UTC - Evidence: deploy timeline shows PR #2894 merged to canary 2026-03-01T08:55Z. Metric correlation: batch_wait_time_p99 jumped from 30-50ms to 1200-2500ms within 10 minutes of that deploy (see dashboard link).

10:45 UTC - Hypothesis B (lower likelihood): KV cache starvation/rehydration causing slower token generation on first requests; looked at kv-miss metrics - small increase but not sufficient to explain p99 magnitude.

11:10 UTC - Experiment: temporarily increased forced flush on batching to 20ms and pinned batch_max_wait_ms to previous value on one canary host; tail latency returned to baseline on that host within 3 minutes.
11:40 UTC - Decision: rollback PR #2894 in canary and roll back to previous batching parameters across affected pool while root-cause verification continues.

root_cause: A recent scheduler change (PR #2894) adjusted the continuous-batching timer and corner-case logic for low-concurrency tails. Under certain traffic patterns on dedicated pools (short prompts, bursty small concurrency per host) the change allowed the batching timer to exceed expected windows, causing small batches to wait long periods before flush. This produced large increases in batch_wait_time and consequently p95/p99 latency and some client timeouts.
resolution: Immediate mitigation: rolled back PR #2894 from affected canary and backfilled previous batching parameters across the nimbus-prod-us-east dedicated pool (completed 2026-03-01T11:35Z). Applied a temporary forced flush at 20ms for short-prompt routes. Customer confirmed improvement and reduced timeouts.
mitigation_and_rollback_steps: 1) Identified offending PR and affected canary hosts
2) Rolled back PR #2894 to previous commit on canary pool
3) Applied temporary batch_max_wait_ms override (20ms) on customer route and redeployed config to pool
4) Monitored metrics for 30m and validated p95/p99 returned to baseline
5) Notified customer and scheduled maintenance window for permanent fix rollout
